title: Divergence: forge::check aborts mutual-recursion termination rejection as a VIR environment error (exit 2, no cert) instead of REQ-6 'rejected there, no crash'

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content:
Failing test (pinned, #[ignore]d) at forge/tests/divergence_mutual_recursion.rs::divergence_mutual_recursion_is_rejected_not_crashed.

DIVERGENCE: .design/basis/10-recursion-tuples.md REQ-6 (+ Architecture + the REQ-2 validator doc-comment) promise a mutually-recursive pair without a dec chain 'reaches Verus and is rejected there (no false L3, no crash)'. forge::check::classify_verus_outcome (forge/src/check.rs) maps Verus's termination rejection 'recursive function must have a decreases clause' (encountered-vir-error: true) to ForgeError::VerusOutput — an ENVIRONMENT abort: exit 2, EMPTY --json stdout, NO certificate. That is a crash in the design's sense (no verdict produced).

CONTRAST (authority, R-CHAR-3): the SAME termination-failure class on a SINGLE self-recursive fn whose dec does not decrease yields a clean parseable L0 cert (exit 0) — recursion_conformance.rs::nondecreasing_recursion_is_l0, REQ-4/AC-2. The mutual case must likewise produce a non-L3 certificate verdict (reject/L0), not an uninterpretable VIR abort.

Probe (real verus 0.2026.05.24):
  fn a(n) { b(n-1) } / fn b(n) { a(n-1) }  no dec, fx pure
  -> forge check --json: exit 2, stdout empty, stderr 'could not interpret verus output: verus reported an internal (VIR) error; ... recursive function must have a decreases clause'

NON-laundering holds (not L3) — the divergence is the 'no crash' clause + the §5.1/R-SPEC-3 'certificate is the deliverable' contract.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Fix landed (forge/src/check.rs, single file): generalize the validator's DIRECT self-call rule (REQ-2, block_calls_name) to a CALL-GRAPH CYCLE. New fn mutual_recursion_cycle_fns reuses closure::reachable_in_file_fns — f is in a mutual cycle iff it shares an SCC (size >= 2) with some other fn g (g reachable from f AND f reachable from g). Pure direct self-recursion (f->f) excluded (REQ-2, dec-supported); fx diverge exempt (#88). The per-item loop emits Certificate::rejected (L0, MutualRecursionUnsupported) per cycle member BEFORE lowering/verus — a parseable verdict-in-cert (no false L3, no crash), matching the single-fn non-decreasing L0 precedent (REQ-4/AC-2), instead of the prior ForgeError::VerusOutput VIR-crash. Pinned test un-ignored + passing.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: RESOLVED in commit 43a5798 (forge/src/check.rs, +114/-4). Root cause: classify_verus_outcome mapped the mutual pair's encountered-vir-error to ForgeError::VerusOutput (exit 2, empty --json stdout, no cert). Fix: catch the mutual-recursion CYCLE at forge check BEFORE lowering/verus (mutual_recursion_cycle_fns — generalizes the validator's direct self-call rule to an SCC test via closure::reachable_in_file_fns; fx diverge exempt #88; whole class, not just the reported pair) and emit Certificate::rejected (L0, MutualRecursionUnsupported) per member — a parseable verdict-in-cert matching the single-fn non-decreasing L0 precedent (REQ-4/AC-2). Verified real verus 0.2026.05.24: pinned divergence_mutual_recursion_is_rejected_not_crashed PASSES (parseable cert array, neither a nor b is L3 — no false L3, no crash); recursion_conformance UNCHANGED (L3/L0/structured-error/L1); cargo test --workspace 628 passed 0 failed 0 ignored; check_conformance 6 passed; clippy + fmt clean. Hand back for acto-critic re-audit.
